A 41-year-old man with a medical history of heart failure, coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive
pulmonary disease, and prostate cancer presents with complaints of palpitations. He has been
hospitalized multiple times recently for decompensated heart failure, requiring intravenous diuretics
and adjustments to his cardiac medications. During his most recent hospitalization one month ago, he
experienced ventricular tachycardia and subsequently had an automated implantable
cardioverter-defibrillator (AICD) placed. He was also started on amiodarone therapy. Since being
discharged four weeks ago, the patient reports fatigue, occasional palpitations, and worsening
lower-extremity edema. He denies chest pain, lightheadedness, orthopnea, changes in exercise
tolerance, tremor, diarrhea, constipation, anxiety, or heat or cold intolerance. He has gained 2.5 kg
over the past month. His current medications include aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg daily,
extended-release metoprolol 100 mg daily, lisinopril 40 mg daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily,
furosemide 20 mg daily, amiodarone 200 mg daily, inhaled tiotropium 18 μg daily, and inhaled albuterol
as needed. On physical examination, his blood pressure is 103/72 mm Hg, heart rate is 65 beats per
minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. He is 178
cm tall, weighs 86 kg (BMI: 27.1), and has 1+ pitting edema to the mid-shin, warm extremities, and
minimal bibasilar crackles. Laboratory results are as follows: | | Patient value | Reference range | | --- |

0.8–1.8 | | Total triiodothyronine (ng/dL) | 55 | 60–181 | Interrogation of his AICD reveals frequent
episodes of nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. What is the most appropriate next step in managing
this patient’s thyroid function abnormalities? Answer Choices: (A) Measure the thyroid-stimulating
immunoglobulin level (B) Obtain thyroid ultrasound with color flow Doppler (C) Start beta-blocker
therapy for thyroid dysfunction (D) Refer for radioactive iodine uptake testing (E) Repeat thyroid
